findings.title: getLoginPredicate NPEs when an IDP has a null config map
findings.body: The new clause in getLoginPredicate calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) whenever idp.getOrganizationId() != null. IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() can be null (e.g. models built programmatically or deserialized without a config map; other code in the codebase null-guards getConfig()). Any create/update/remove of an IDP that is linked to an organization but has a null config will now throw a NullPointerException inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, breaking the write operation. Guard with idp.getConfig() == null || ... instead.

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal string "alias" rather than the constructed alias variable ("idp-alias-" + i). The registered cleanup will target a non-existent identity provider and either throw 404 during cleanup or silently fail, leaking the 20 created IDPs between test runs and potentially making subsequent runs fail on alias conflicts. The same bug exists at line 425 for "idp-alias-20".

findings.title: Cached getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering
findings.body: When served from cache, getForLogin collects the IDPs into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(), whereas the uncached/delegate path returns the delegate's stream, which for the JPA storage is ordered by alias. Callers that sort (like IdentityProviderBean) are unaffected, but any other consumer of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relies on the ordering of the delegate (a behavioral difference between cached and uncached invocations) will see non-deterministic ordering only when the cache is warm. Use a LinkedHashSet or sort before returning to keep behavior consistent.
